mainTopic: Where the chambers of the בית המוקד stood: settling the contradiction between מסכת תמיד and מסכת מידות about the לשכת הטלאים
overview: This amud continues a contradiction about the chambers of the בית המוקד. מסכת תמיד places the chamber of the lambs (לשכת הטלאים) in the northwest corner, but מסכת מידות places it in the southwest corner. First, the גמרא concludes that מסכת מידות follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, so the two משניות come from different authorities. Then רב אדא בריה דרב יצחק gives another answer: the chamber was not in a corner at all. It sat along the western wall, so it looked 'south' to someone coming from the north and 'north' to someone coming from the south. The גמרא adds that the chamber was probably closer to the southwest corner. As proof, it recalls a similar contradiction about the chamber where the לחם הפנים was prepared. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע resolved that contradiction by saying one משנה counts the chambers going to the right and the other counts going to the left.

steps.title: The משנה in מסכת מידות follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the משנה in מסכת מידות follows the view of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. This settles the contradiction by assigning the two משניות to different authors.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not conclude from this that it is the view of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב? Yes, conclude from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up its earlier discussion. It decides that the משנה in מסכת מידות was taught according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two משניות disagree about where the לשכת הטלאים was. Once one of them is attributed to a specific תנא, the conflict becomes a real disagreement between authors and not a contradiction inside one source. The closing words 'שמע מינה' confirm the conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not so that... (introduces a forced conclusion)
Learn from it / conclude from it
A תנא known for his precise reports about the Temple's layout

steps.whatToRemember: The first answer to the contradiction: מסכת מידות follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, so the two משניות come from different authorities.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not conclude from it,
that it is the view of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov?

phrases.notes: The גמרא agrees with the point, and that wraps up this part of the discussion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion carried over earlier about which תנא authored מסכת מידות.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מסכת מידות reflects the view of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

steps.title: The chamber stood along the wall, not in a corner
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בריה דרב יצחק offers another way to resolve the contradiction. The לשכת הטלאים was set back from the corner, along the middle of the western side. So it looked 'south' to someone coming from the north, and 'north' to someone coming from the south.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בריה דרב יצחק said: This chamber was set off from the corner. To one who comes from the north it looks like it is in the south, and to one who comes from the south it looks like it is in the north.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא gives a different answer to the contradiction about the לשכת הטלאים. In his answer, both משניות are correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer said the two משניות disagree. רב אדא says they describe the same room from two different viewpoints. Since the room was not in a corner but along the western wall, 'north' and 'south' depend on which direction you approach from.

keyTerms.meaning: Chamber / room in the Temple complex
It was cut off / set apart (from the corner)

steps.confusionAlert: רב אדא is not saying the משניות disagree about the facts. He is saying they agree on the location and only describe it from different angles.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַדָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יִצְחָק אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Adda, son of Rav Yitzchak, said:
This chamber was set off (from the corner),
and for one who comes from the north,
it appears to him to be in the south;
and for one who comes from the south,
it appears to him to be in the north.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַדָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יִצְחָק אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the same contradiction, without needing two different authors.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reconciliation by perspective: one location described from two vantage points
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משניות truly disagree about where the chamber stood (north corner versus south corner).
steps.terutzMaskana: The chamber was along the western wall, away from the corners, so both descriptions fit.

steps.title: The chamber leaned toward the southwest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that, even on רב אדא's approach, the chamber was more likely closer to the southwest corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is reasonable that it was in the southwest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a point about where exactly the chamber sat. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא placed the chamber along the western side. The גמרא now says it was not exactly in the middle but closer to the southern end. A proof is about to be given.

phrases.english: And it is reasonable to say
that it was in the southwest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רב אדא's picture: the chamber leaned toward the south.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The לשכת הטלאים sat closer to the southwest corner.

steps.title: The proof begins: the shewbread contradiction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the chamber leaned southwest. It points to a similar contradiction between the משניות about the chamber where the לחם הפנים was prepared.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? From the fact that we raise a contradiction between one משנה about the shewbread and another משנה about the shewbread,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its proof. It recalls another known contradiction between מסכת תמיד and מסכת מידות, this time about the לחם הפנים chamber.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מסכת תמיד puts the לחם הפנים chamber in the northeast. מסכת מידות puts it in the southeast. The way that contradiction was resolved will show us the layout of the chambers.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? / How do we know?
We raise a contradiction (between two sources)
The shewbread placed on the Table in the Temple

phrases.english: From where do we know this?
From the fact that we contrast the shewbread (chamber)

phrases.notes: מסכת תמיד places it in the northeast; מסכת מידות places it in the southeast.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי — מִדְּרָמֵינַן לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים אַלֶּחֶם הַפָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim made in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That the לשכת הטלאים leaned toward the southwest
steps.raayaSupportSource: The known contradiction between מסכת תמיד and מסכת מידות about the לחם הפנים chamber

steps.title: Counting right versus counting left
steps.stepSummary: The proof is completed with רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's resolution. One משנה lists the chambers moving to the right, and the other lists them moving to the left. This shows that both משניות describe one layout from different directions, which supports the southwest placement.
steps.simpleTranslation: and we resolve it, as רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: One Master counts going by way of the right, and the other Master counts going by way of the left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the answer that resolved the לחם הפנים contradiction and uses it as proof for its claim about the לשכת הטלאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא says מסכת מידות counts the chambers going rightward (south, east, north, west), and מסכת תמיד counts going leftward (south, west, north, east). So 'different corners' really reflects different counting routes around one fixed layout. That layout supports placing the לשכת הטלאים toward the southwest.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master (refers to the author of each משנה)
By way of the right / by way of the left

steps.whatToRemember: The two משניות can agree on where things stood and still list them differently, because they go around the room in opposite directions. This idea supports the southwest placement of the לשכת הטלאים.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common way the גמרא settles apparent contradictions about the Temple layout: by asking from which direction each source describes the room.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: as Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
One Master counts going by way of the right,
and the other Master counts going by way of the left.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְשַׁנֵּינַן, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 4 by quoting the accepted resolution of the לחם הפנים contradiction.
steps.raayaObject: That the לשכת הטלאים was toward the southwest
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's resolution: the משניות count the chambers in opposite directions
